text:
jess_support: FYI escalation from customer (acme-payments): intermittent 403s and TLS handshake failures when calling our private endpoint via their VPC endpoint. Failures spike under concurrency. They see curl succeed sometimes but our SDK gets 403 / TLS alerts. Attaching their brief logs below and asking for network checks:

jess_support: customer says their app -> corporate proxy -> TGW -> VPCE -> our NLB. They suspect proxy. Logs: 
```
> 2026-03-01T14:12:03Z ERROR request failed status=403 tls: handshake error: remote error: tls: bad certificate
> 2026-03-01T14:12:03Z INFO conn client_ip=10.2.5.12:45678 dst=vpce-0abcdef1234ec2.internal:443 SNI=
```

raj_net: quick thought — that log line shows SNI empty. Corporate proxy or TLS terminator likely stripping SNI or doing MITM TLS inspection without reissuing a matching cert. Two things to confirm from customer: their TCP-level view of the ClientHello (tcpdump/pcap) and DNS resolution path. Ask them to run these from an affected EC2 in the same subnet as the app: 
```
# verify DNS resolution for our hostname from the app host
dig +short api.redwood-internal.example.com @169.254.169.253
# confirm it resolves to the VPCE ENI IP(s)
# tcpdump capture for TLS ClientHello (first few packets)
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -s 0 -w /tmp/tls.pcap 'tcp port 443 and (((ip src host <app_ip>) and (ip dst host <vpce_eni_ip>)) or (host <vpce_eni_ip>))' & sleep 10; pkill -f tcpdump
# openssl peek to see servername being sent by client
openssl s_client -connect api.redwood-internal.example.com:443 -servername api.redwood-internal.example.com -brief
```

maria_engineer: also ask them to run an openssl client WITHOUT -servername to demonstrate missing SNI: 
```
# missing-sni test (simulate proxy stripping SNI)
printf '' | openssl s_client -connect api.redwood-internal.example.com:443 -quiet 2>&1 | sed -n '1,40p'
```
If that returns the expected Redwood cert only when -servername is present, it's SNI-related.

tim_sre: another angle — NAT ephemeral port exhaustion or SNAT churn can cause upstream connections to appear from many ports/ips and break connection reuse. Under concurrency the corporate proxy or NAT-GW may run out and start failing with 403 from our side if their requests end up routed through an intermediate that doesn't forward SNI. Ask them to check ephemeral port usage on their NAT device and the number of simultaneous outbound flows. Simple repro to show port exhaustion: 
```
# from a linux host, spin up many short-lived connections
for i in {1..2000}; do timeout 2 bash -c "echo > /dev/tcp/api.redwood-internal.example.com/443" & done; wait
# then check conntrack / netstat
sudo ss -natp | grep :443 | wc -l
sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count
```

jess_support: Customer ran quick checks and posted results: they resolved our host to 10.10.7.23 (vpce ENI), tcpdump shows ClientHello with no server_name extension in many samples, and their proxy logs show TLS_INSPECT=true. They also saw conntrack near capacity on their edge NAT.

raj_net: ok confirmed — two independent issues likely compounding: 1) TLS inspection/proxy removing SNI or reissuing a cert that doesn't match our api hostname, and 2) ephemeral port / conntrack limits causing retries and fallback paths that hit another proxy that doesn't forward SNI. Root cause = SNI stripping + SNAT exhaustion causing requests to be routed via a different inspection appliance.

maria_engineer: mitigation options (short term):
- Ask customer's network/security team to enable TLS passthrough for our host or configure their inspection appliance to preserve SNI and not reissue certs for this host.
- Add VPCE ENI IPs (10.10.7.23 etc.) to their proxy/firewall allowlist to bypass inspection for our traffic.
- Increase conntrack / ephemeral port pool on NAT/GW and use connection reuse / keepalives in their SDK.

maria_engineer: repro steps we shared for them to demonstrate fix locally: 
```
# bypass proxy and hit ENI directly (works = good)
curl -v --connect-to api.redwood-internal.example.com:443:10.10.7.23 https://api.redwood-internal.example.com/health
# test SNI present (should return our cert CN=api.redwood-internal.example.com)
openssl s_client -connect 10.10.7.23:443 -servername api.redwood-internal.example.com
```
deploybot: canary check at 14:10Z failed 1/3 with TLS handshake error to that customer's VPCE IP (10.10.7.23) — seen in logs: `tls: client did not send SNI`.

tim_sre: longer-term: suggest using dedicated private deployment (pins certs on their side) or adding a private TLS-terminating ALB inside their VPC with trust relationship if they must inspect traffic. Also recommend they enable keepalives and client-side connection pooling to reduce ephemeral port churn.

jess_support: next steps assigned:
- customer-network team to whitelist VPCE ENI IPs and reconfigure TLS inspector (action: customer)
- we will provide explicit list of VPCE ENI IPs and sample openssl/curl commands for validation (action: jess_support + maria_engineer)
- customer to validate conntrack/ephemeral port capacity and increase if needed (action: customer)

jess_support: customer verified that bypassing proxy (allowlist) fixed the 403s and TLS errors in their staging test. They will schedule a maintenance window to update proxy rules. Closing loop once they confirm prod cutover. :thumbsup:
